column3: INFO-BACKLOG PREDICTIVE STUDY — does a desk's UNCONSUMED info backlog PREDICT anything? WALTER's design, PROME-docketed 2026-09-11: WQ-206's aged-ACTION-line grant is action-keyed BY DESIGN (info is not an obligation), so an info stack trips NO gate at any size — LIQUID is the live instance (28 unconsumed in inbox/WALTER, ZERO of them action-class, desk dark since 9/03, last drain 9/03). DELIBERATELY NOT a threshold: picking a bar tonight encodes a guess and manufactures drain work on a category we have correctly ruled non-obligating. The study instead measures whether backlog size/age at a desk PREDICTS a later correction, a stale-figure dispatch AGAINST that desk, or a reconcile. ⛔ NULL ARM CORRECTED 2026-09-11 19:1x (WALTER self-reported, Codex-flagged; the original wording was WALTER's, adopted by PROME nearly verbatim and therefore PROME's to fix): the original said 'predicts nothing ⇒ info is PROVEN free and we stop looking'. That is an OVERCLAIM — absence of a detected relationship is not evidence of no relationship, and a small or inconclusive study cannot establish that unread information has no cost. THE DEFENSIBLE NULL ARM IS A BOUNDED DECISION TO STOP MONITORING UNDER STATED CONDITIONS — n, which desks, what window, what effect size the study could have detected — never a proof of costlessness. ⚠️ WALTER's own note on why the bad version was attractive, worth keeping: 'we stop looking' is what makes a null result feel worth funding, which is exactly the pressure that inflates it; the honest version is less satisfying and is the one that survives someone asking what n was. Predicts corrections ⇒ a leading indicator, and THEN it earns a bar, sized from the data.
